Director’s Message

Director’s MessageVisionHistoryDirections

(AI-drafted) Draft · under revision

We have the capability, the vision and the system to turn the dream of robots into reality.

Thank you for visiting Seoul National University Robotics Institute. I often think about where a good robot begins. The answer I have come to is that it begins not with a technology but with a question. Only once we decide whose problem we are solving, and which problem, can we design the body and the intelligence that fit it. That is why we set out to build robots for people, not robots that merely resemble people.

The places where this question matters most are close to home. In a super-aged society, more and more people who need care themselves end up caring for someone else. What this reality calls for is not intelligence that stays on a screen but robots that lend real physical help, close to people’s bodies and in the spaces where they live. This is why the Institute has put robots that support daily life, wearable robots, and medical robots that help diagnose and treat from inside the body at the center of its research.

Robots used this close to people cannot be built with the knowledge of a single field. We have to consider not only how well a robot performs but also the body of the person using it, the setting they live in, and their safety. That is why more than 80 researchers from engineering, medicine, public health, brain and cognitive sciences, clothing and textiles, and the social sciences work together at the Institute. By convergence we do not mean everyone doing the same work toward the same goal. We mean one researcher’s idea being applied in a new way by another, and that result in turn moving yet another line of research.

A good idea, however, does not by itself become a good robot. Robots get better by being built, used in the field, and redesigned around the problems that use reveals, again and again. It is hard for an individual lab to carry this cycle alone. The Institute therefore provides a shared foundation for turning ideas into real robots and testing them, works with hospitals to confirm that they help, and opens a path from research results to commercialization and start-ups.

In the end, what we want to build is not one robot or one technology but an ecosystem in which good robots keep being born. Students learn by making things themselves; that experience becomes research; research is put to use in society; and what is learned there returns to education and research. Our selection as a National Research Lab allows us to concentrate on this work for the next ten years. We will make this a place that outstanding people want to come to.

I hope that what none of us could do alone, we can now do together. We ask for your interest and participation in the road ahead for SNU Robotics Institute.

Kyu-Jin Cho
Director, SNU Robotics Institute
